title: 9.66J Computational Cognitive Science (Fall 2004)
authors: Joshua B. Tenenbaum (instructor; slide author per PDF metadata)
description: Undergraduate introduction to computational theories of human cognition: the problem of induction, knowledge representation, Bayesian inference, graphical models, concept learning and categorization, Occam's razor, hierarchical models, intuitive theories and causal learning. OCW publishes the syllabus, calendar, readings list, 24 lecture slide decks (PDF), study materials and two example student projects.
rightsNotes: Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 by MIT OpenCourseWare (the course page links the licence; the OCW terms of use apply). Attribution and share-alike are required; commercial use is excluded. Corniversity is private and non-commercial.

Many slides state 'Image removed due to copyright considerations'; the published PDFs omit third-party figures, including the human generalization data plots of the number game. Corniversity does not reconstruct or quote the removed material.
The readings page is bibliographic only (no open PDFs; some 'Buy at MIT Press' links). Readings are reference-only and are not imported.
This is the Fall 2004 offering. The current MIT course (9.66J/9.660/6.804J, CBMM page) has no public materials; see the mit-cognitive-science record.

syllabus: two 1.5-hour lectures per week; prerequisite 'a class in probability or statistics'; programming experience desirable; no single required text; four problem sets and a final project or paper; grading 40% problem sets, 40% project, 20% discussion
calendar: 25 sessions with problem-set and project milestones
lecture notes index: 24 slide decks (sessions 1–24; session 25 is project presentations with no file)

lecture PDFs text-extracted: sept_9_2004.pdf (72 pp.), sept_14_2004.pdf (65 pp.), oct_5_2004_final.pdf (44 pp.), oct_14_2004_fin.pdf (67 pp.), oct_19_2004_fin.pdf (53 pp.), oct_21_2004_fin.pdf (49 pp.); oct_12_2004_fin.pdf (47 pp.) extracted and found to contain Bayes-net material
readings page (bibliographic citations only), projects page (guidelines and two example projects as PDFs), study materials (MATLAB notes and a statistics/regression handout)
limitations: Slide decks, not prose notes: many slides are figures or one-line titles, and copyrighted images are removed. Lessons must supply the derivations the slides only gesture at.
Page-level locators exist only for the seven decks whose text was extracted (lectures 1, 2, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13); the other decks have file-level locators only.

The file names and the listed lecture topics do not always align: oct_12_2004_fin.pdf (listed as 'Simple Bayesian Learning 1') contains Bayes-net semantics, explaining away and sampling; oct_14_2004_fin.pdf (listed as 'Simple Bayesian Learning 2') contains Bayesian parameter estimation, hierarchical priors and MCMC; oct_19_2004_fin.pdf opens with MCMC and topic models before concepts and categories. Locators record what the pages actually contain.
Printed page labels are present only in oct_5, oct_19 and oct_21 (equal to physical index + 1); the other decks have no printed labels.
Material is from 2004; later developments (probabilistic programming, large-scale models) are covered through the probmods-v2 record, not this one.
